title: Proactive capacity guardrails and graceful eviction for dedicated fleet upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Upgrades to dedicated GPU pools currently risk transient capacity loss and request queueing when nodes are drained. Existing drain logic causes autoscaler to react by spinning up new nodes or allowing sudden evictions that increase tail latency and cost. We need a reproducible, capacity-aware upgrade flow that combines rollout gates, LTS channel semantics, and coordinated autoscaler controls to ensure no-customer-impact upgrades for Dedicated customers.

Goals: 1) Implement a proactive capacity guardrail that prevents a drain operation from reducing available serving slots below a configurable threshold per pool (e.g., 15% headroom). 2) Add a "graceful eviction shepherd" component that sequences pod/node evacuation by prioritizing low-utilization placements, migrating warm KV caches, and prewarming replacement nodes before traffic shifts. 3) Extend rollout gates to include autoscaler-aware checks (scale-state, pending-provisioning, GPU prewarm status) so a canary can only proceed if capacity metrics are healthy. 4) Bake these behaviors into our LTS channel tooling so customers on LTS receive staged, safe rollouts with rollback hooks.

Non-goals: Changed pricing model or altering global autoscaler policies unrelated to upgrades.

Key design decisions: - Introduce a pool-level "min-headroom" config that the upgrade controller queries before initiating drains. That value is set per-customer or per-GPU-pool. - Avoid hard drain blasts: perform drains in micro-batches (default 2 nodes at a time) and delay subsequent batches until target metrics stabilize for a configurable window. - Coordinate with autoscaler via a handshake API: the controller requests node prewarm and waits for a "ready-for-eviction" signal. We will implement exponential backoff for prewarm failures and an automated rollback if prewarm does not complete within the SLA. - LTS rollouts get a stricter gate (higher headroom and longer stabilization windows).

Observability and guards: Primary metrics to gate on include available_slots, pooled_kv_hit_rate, p95_token_latency, inflight_request_count, and pending_nodes_count. Add a rollout dashboard and alert that surfaces when headroom drops below threshold or when drain-induced evictions increase error-rate by >2x.

Runbook highlights: 1) If canary causes degraded p95 latency, abort and trigger rollback to previous runtime image. 2) If autoscaler oscillation is observed, engage "static-hold" mode to block new scale actions (manual override) and notify infra on-call.

Deliverables: design doc link, controller implementation, autoscaler handshake API, LTS rollout integration, end-to-end canary job pipeline, dashboards, and an updated incident runbook.
